profile.headline: Software Engineer at Meta
profile.summary:
I have developed tools and utilities for Professional Artists and Software Development environments. My experience spans work in movie production environments, through commercial software engineering and commercial services. My career has steered me through corporate America as well as many start-ups. 

I have always and will always enjoy working on software for the sake of making a persons life just a little bit easier. Mostly accomplished through tools, but occasionally found in services and client applications.

Specialties: Cloud Services, Service Oriented Software, C++, Java, Perl, Batch Processing, Web Development, Video On Demand Client software.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Ewa Beach, Hawaii, United States · Remote
positions.description: If you don't know what Meta (The company formerly known as Facebook) is, then I am not sure I can describe it well enough to give it justice.  Not sure exactly what I'll be doing, but I am looking forward to the social challenge ahead.  Don't forget to like this description and subscribe.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
The first question which seems to always come to people's minds is: 'What is Grab?"  the best answer I seem to come up with is: "It's the Uber of South-East Asia"  While not a perfect comparison, I'll stick with that until someone follows up with "What is Uber?"

I have acclimated and had my head in the clouds for a year now.  Time to get down to earth.  (The Columbia Center...  it's a pretty tall building)

positions.title: Senior Staff Engineer
positions.description: This is a place where people work on "awesome" and carry swords while doing it.   (This is not metaphorical, there are real sword props)  Have been working on different platforms, Android TV, Android Mobile, Xbox 360, Fire TV, PS4, etc.  Got a chance to switch over to work on HBO.com (the website) and also got to organize the company sanctioned hack'a'thon (Alt-Shift).   Dodged swords and deadlines.  Explored Westeros and Westworld...  now it's time to find a new place to roll.

positions.title: Software Engineer - OS Spelunker
positions.description:
Making awesome things in an awesome environment with awesome people who think awesome thoughts. Worked on a few very ambitious things and had great discussions with really smart and hard working people.  Met and worked with more landmark people than any other time in my career.

Unfortunately, I cannot fill out my resume here, as all of it is confidential, but all in good time.

positions.title: Senior Software Development Engineer - Living Room Experience
positions.description:
I have become a Huligan as the company likes to put it. 

Working on the Living Room Experience team. Already had a chance to bring the PS3 client and the WiiU to production. Continuing to work on next generation product/clients. Totally awesome!!!

Year 2013 mission complete, and I've had a chance to launch the new Samsung TV and BluRay experience, the LG TV experience, Sony BluRay and the PlayStation 4. worked on a couple of updates to WiiU and PS3 and had an itty bitty hand in Wii and Roku releases as well.

Tenure over, Mission Complete.

positions.title: Software Dev Engineer II - Video Games
positions.description:
I would love to put something here... but it's mostly confidential.  Work rendered will probably be more visible later. 

Responsible for Mobile App Store Financial Reporting, just recently released, so now available to talk about.

I can say the last thing my team did was build the internal infrastructure for the "Test Drive" feature for Amazon's mobile app store.

I have on the other hand mentored quite a few junior engineers, lead multiple teams to launch products and have generally had fun working with the awesome and intelligent people in my division.

positions.title: Software Dev Engineer II - ContraCogs
positions.description:
Was a part of a team known as ContraCogs.  We were responsible for managing the thousands of Amazon.com coop contracts with product vendors.  These contracts would then be translated into over a Billion dollars which vendors owed Amazon for services rendered, such as advertising.

Notable Stuff:
Developed new features on an existing accounting software: ContraCogs.   Had major financial impact easily reaching into the millions of dollars.  

Worked on improving release workflow and overall product quality. (mostly java... perl/mason)

positions.title: Company Founder/Lead Software Engineer
positions.description:
One of the original 4 Company founders. Architect-ed and developed qube!, the companies primary product on a single code base for multiple platforms including Linux, Windows, OSX, Irix and Solaris. 

The company has hundreds of clients spanning thousands of licenses. qube! can be credited for it's use on many major Hollywood productions as well as video game and other verticals.

positions.title: Production Software Engineer
positions.description:
Was a part of an awesome team of Software Developers who supported the production needs of Final Fantasy and subsequently the Animatrix project.

Notable Projects:
Developed the second version of an in-house batch queuing system, SQB 2.0, used on The Animatrix: The Final Flight of the Osiris which proved to be a very successful robust system of which turned into qube!

Developed the first version of an in-house batch queuing system, GUI - Launchpad 1.0, used on Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within movie production, also worked closely with the Render Wrangling groups developing tools to automate and simplify workflow.

positions.title: Computer Technician
positions.description: Troubleshot and Repaired PC and Apple hardware.  I spent lots of time putting together new PC's as well as fixing old ones.   All manner of different brands, Packard Bell, Compaq, Dell, IBM, Apple, etc... etc..  All manners of problems from dead hard drives to viruses.

positions.title: Web Software Engineer
positions.description: Designed, implemented and maintained the citybytes.com website.  Citybytes.com was like many other websites which ventured into building technologies and features which  were quite new at the time.   I had a blast developing CGI based forums and shopping cart technology in "ANSI C".

projects.title: Mobile App Store Sales and Earnings reports
Amazon Appstore Financial Reporting Portal
projects.description:
The Amazon Appstore's financial reporting portal (the place where developers go online to check their earnings) was desperately in need of a revamp.  The existing reporting was comprised of a smallish graph wrapped up in a Flash widget with a date picker -- pretty shabby.  It was time to bring our portal up to par (at least!) with competitive appstore's online portals.

After several months of hard work, we relaunched an impressive single-page HTML5 dashboard, replete with new, easy-to-find features, a pretty new style, and support for the Appstore's new Subscriptions and In-App Purchases features, as well as easy access to PDF reports from previous months and CSVs for arbitrary date ranges and applications.

My personal involvement was mainly in building out the frontend, laying down some of the groundwork before the project was fully under way, and adding some much-needed functionality to our stack (to add a portal/portlet model for components, if you must know!).  We had to cut a lot of features to make our release dates on time, but ultimately we managed without putting in extreme hours, and our developers were delighted, giving us ample positive feedback on the clean design, updated-daily reports, and responsive site.
